text:
maria: FYI ran a targeted nightly perf sweep on the mixed farm. Observed p99 latency spikes for seq_len ~512 workloads on a few nodes. Noticed some odd SM capability detection flips and KV-cache thrash during the run. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

jin: Which nodes + driver? Can you paste the capprobe output and the perf summary?

maria: Nodes: gpu-a12 (sm86), gpu-b03 (sm92), gpu-c07 (sm75). Driver: 535.2 on most, but gpu-b03 ended up with 540.1 for one job. Capprobe snippet from gpu-b03:
```
cap_probe --json
{"device":"gpu-b03","sm":92,"tensor_cores":true,"bf16":true,"fp8":false,"kernel_table":"/opt/redwood/kernels/sm92"}
```
Notice it reports fp8=false but the kernel_table indicates sm92 optimized kernels present. Logs show later fallback to generic kernel after several failed launches.

perf-bot: job_summary 2976543000:
- model: rw-infer-v1
- workload: seq=512, batch=1..8 mixing
- p50=22.1ms p95=78.4ms p99=412.3ms
- batching_rate dropped ~18% mid-run
- kv_cache_hit_rate 0.94 -> 0.88 (evictions spiked)
/artifacts/2976543000/profile.tar.gz

sam: From the profiler (attached): kernel "matmul_sm92_tc_bf16" shows launch overhead ~2.4ms intermittently (should be ~0.9ms) which aligns with the p99 spikes. Also saw the runtime pick "generic_matmul" for some iterations which costs ~1.8x.

maria: I ran a local microbench to repro gating behavior. Results: 
- seq=256 -> kernel K1 (sm92-tc) median=12ms
- seq=512 -> kernel K2 (generic) median=34ms
So the sequence-length gating seems to route 512 to the non-optimized path on these nodes. We recently changed the seqlen gating threshold in canary from 384 -> 256; could that be related?

dmitri: We did push a conservative gating change because of a previous regression on mixed farms. But we also added a capability flag check that treats fp8 support as optional if kernel_table exists. Maybe the flag logic is too permissive: if fp8=false but kernel_table exists, we still route to tc path. If the kernel binaries aren't fully compatible with the driver, launch can fail and runtime falls back (costly).

maria: Also saw KV cache eviction logs around the same time which look like thrash: the KV manager got a surge of invalidation requests leading to simultaneous GC across shards. Snippet:
```
kv_cache: eviction_triggered shard=3 reason=stale_index count=432
kv_cache: eviction_complete shard=3 duration_ms=1427
kv_cache: backpressure_applied=false
```
That long GC + no backpressure means many inflight requests hit fallback code paths.

sam: So two contributing factors: (1) capability flags/kerneltable mismatch causing unstable kernel launches, (2) seqlen gating change + KV thrash causing more work serialized on fallback paths.

perf-bot: autotune probe results (first-warmup microbench):
- node gpu-b03: probe_success=false (2/10 warmup launches failed)
- node gpu-a12: probe_success=true (10/10)
- historic: nodes with probe_success=false show 2.1x p99 regressed

jin: Quick suggestion: add a runtime probe that does a lightweight kernel microbench (10 small launches) on initial attach and mark the node's capability as "verified" only if probe_success==true. That avoids optimistic routing to tensor-core paths just because kernel files exist. Also log driver+cuda runtime mismatch explicitly.

dmitri: Agreed. Also we should roll back the seqlen gating change on canary to 384 so seq=512 stays on the optimized fastpath until we validate the probe. I'll own the revert PR.

sam: I'll look at KV cache eviction pressure — quick mitigation: set backpressure_applied=true when concurrent_evictions>2 to slow incoming requests and avoid giant GC waves. I'll open a small patch and run the unit test.

maria: Action items (from thread):
1) jin -> implement initial-launch microbench probe + mark kernel_verified flag (priority P0).
2) dmitri -> revert seqlen gating change on canary (P0).
3) sam -> KV cache backpressure tweak and small integration test (P1).
4) maria -> coordinate canary rollback and open incident note + perf dashboard alert for p99 spike.

maria: I'll also attach a short playbook for operators: if p99>300ms for seq512 workloads: set canary gating to 384, disable optimistic tc routing on nodes with probe_success=false, and restart runtime on affected nodes. :clipboard: :ambulance:

jin: I'll start the probe PR today. One more data point: we should also record the exact kernel binary checksum in the capprobe output (so we can correlate a bad binary with failures).

perf-bot: acknowledged. Will add kernel_sha256 to next probe output.

maria: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after we have probe telemetry from the next nightly run. If anyone sees the p99 still climbing after the revert, ping here and I'll escalate. :pray:
